kind: Proposed decomposition of existing functional requirements

requirements.FR-01: The framework shall retain each requirement with its identifier, revision, statement, product level, source and parent revisions, rationale, owner, conditions or quantities, applicable units, verification method, criterion and resolution status, including reasons for unresolved or inapplicable fields.
requirements.FR-02: The framework shall check created or edited requirement drafts on each edit or request for declared deterministic quality errors, probable semantic duplicates, coverage gaps and source conflicts, returning affected text or records, the rule or cited passage, corrective suggestions or questions, uncertainty and assessment limits.
requirements.FR-03: The framework shall recommend derivation, analysis, verification and validation methods or models on edits or requests using the current lifecycle stage, engineering question, requirements, available inputs, validity, resources and scope, with applicability conditions, rationale, cited sources, alternatives and rejection records.
requirements.FR-04: The framework shall retrieve forward and reverse links among expectations, ConOps scenarios, requirements, function and element allocations, interfaces, decisions and applicable evidence, reporting missing or ambiguous endpoints and coverage against the declared reference set.
requirements.FR-17: The framework shall produce proposed EPS and component requirement allocations from identified spacecraft requirements, scenarios and sourced design quantities using a declared derivation method, retaining parent links, units, assumptions, uncertainty and engineer dispositions.
requirements.FR-29: The framework shall retain the authorized engineer disposition of each requirement correction or method/model suggestion as accepted, modified, rejected or deferred, with rationale and the exact suggestion and context revisions.
requirements.FR-30: The framework shall mark affected assistance stale when its requirement, mission, design, source, criterion or scope revision changes.
requirements.FR-45: The framework shall block the application of stale suggestions as current guidance.
requirements.FR-46: The framework shall initiate reassessment of affected assistance for the new context when its requirement, mission, design, source, criterion or scope revision changes.
requirements.FR-39: The framework shall propose next engineering activities and repeated assessments from the declared phase, product maturity, dependencies, open findings and review criteria, identifying unmet prerequisites and the rationale for each proposal.
requirements.FR-41: The framework shall acknowledge each assistance trigger for the current context within the engineer-approved acknowledgement limit.
requirements.FR-47: The framework shall return a finding, recommendation or explicit pending/unavailable status for each assistance trigger and current context within the engineer-approved interactive response limit.
requirements.FR-48: The framework shall record the trigger, acknowledgement, first-response and completion times of each assistance exchange with its exact context revision.
requirements.FR-25: The framework shall retain mission expectations, constraints and nominal/degraded ConOps scenarios with mission/scenario identity, configuration, orbit, attitude, duration, environmental conditions, subsystem modes, load schedules and transitions as revision-linked inputs to EPS requirements and analysis.
requirements.FR-15: The framework shall configure EPS design representations through identified parameters, component variants and extensions covering generation, storage, conversion, regulation, protection, distribution, control, interfaces and requirement allocations.
requirements.FR-13: The framework shall calculate revision-linked EPS mass, occupied volume and stack-height estimates from aggregate or component design data and assess margins against allocations, retaining sources, units, aggregation assumptions, uncertainty and unknown values.
requirements.FR-14: The framework shall compare EPS concepts and architectures through common feasibility checks and parameter sensitivity assessments covering applicable choices of cell technology, array/battery series and parallel configurations, bus voltage, direct energy transfer or maximum power point tracking, and buck/boost regulation, reporting raw measures, margins, uncertainty, risks and preference ranking under engineer-approved criteria.
requirements.FR-20: The framework shall calculate nominal and peak mode power, conversion/distribution losses, sunlight/eclipse energy budgets, and beginning/end-of-life array and battery sizing, including efficiencies, duty cycles, illumination, temperature, degradation, cycle life, allowable depth of discharge and engineer-defined margins, reporting integer cell counts, series/parallel arrangements, array area, battery capacity and allocation/operating-limit findings.
requirements.FR-16: The framework shall execute EPS analyses covering mission energy balance and survival autonomy, photovoltaic I--V/P--V characteristics, converter/regulator responses, conversion/distribution losses, battery voltage and state of charge, electrothermal behavior, SOH prediction with uncertainty indicators, conducted emissions and stress on protection components. It shall apply time-dependent loads, schedules, mode transitions and supplied orbit, attitude, illumination, eclipse and thermal conditions, reporting histories, dissipation, energy shortages and margins against declared electrical, battery, thermal, emission and component-rating limits.
requirements.FR-18: The framework shall exchange identified EPS and external spacecraft/subsystem models through declared electrical, thermal, applicable EMC and geometry profiles with directions, entity/channel mappings, quantities, units, model/tool revisions, supported effects, execution status and unsupported or lossy transfers.
requirements.FR-43: The framework shall map incoming spacecraft/subsystem conditions, constraints and feasibility findings from identified NVIDIA Omniverse scenarios to framework-executed EPS analyses under the declared coupling profile, preserving mission/scenario identity, configuration and coupling-profile revisions, directions, entity/channel mappings, quantities, units, model/tool revisions, supported effects, execution status and unsupported or lossy transfers.
requirements.FR-44: The framework shall return computed EPS states, dissipation, margins and feasibility findings to the same identified NVIDIA Omniverse scenario and configuration under the declared coupling profile, preserving mission/scenario identity, configuration and coupling-profile revisions, directions, entity/channel mappings, quantities, units, model/tool revisions, supported effects, execution status and unsupported or lossy transfers.
requirements.FR-21: The framework shall assess each model-supported conclusion against intended use, numerical checks, validity limits, uncertainty and engineer-approved prediction-error rules, retaining selected fidelity, included/omitted mechanisms, calibration evidence, independent assessment evidence or explicit gaps, and the resulting credibility findings. It shall distinguish uncertainty indicators and diagnostic scores from calibrated probabilities.
requirements.FR-22: The framework shall estimate photovoltaic, battery electrical/electrothermal and dynamic EPS/load model parameters from quality-checked supplied data under declared fitting criteria, producing controlled, revision-linked calibration proposals and retaining prior/revised values, residuals, uncertainty and affected analyses separately from independent assessment.
requirements.FR-23: The framework shall retain the fidelity, solver and coupling configuration, time step, convergence rules, execution environment, required resources and estimated/measured runtime for each analysis, MIL or SIL run, with unmet resource or numerical limits reported.
requirements.FR-26: The framework shall identify applicable EPS RAM analyses covering failure modes, effects and criticality, conditional failure scenarios and combinations, failure propagation, reliability and redundancy, service availability and modeled restoration, retaining chosen measures, failure dependencies, probability/rate and recovery assumptions, coverage and reasons for exclusions.
requirements.FR-27: The framework shall generate and execute applicable EPS RAM representations for the analyses in FR-26 using identified functions, components, failure dependencies and declared representation rules, assessing failure effects, qualitative/quantitative criticality, minimal failure combinations, conditional failure probabilities, mission reliability, redundancy and time-dependent modeled service availability against declared criteria. It shall assess modeled detection, isolation, reconfiguration and restoration outcomes and retain sourced parameters, service/recovery assumptions, uncertainty and missing-data findings. Missing failure or recovery data shall leave affected quantitative results unavailable.
requirements.FR-31: The framework shall retain and check scenario time bases, sample and receipt times, sampling, synchronization and known calculation/interface delays for simulated or supplied reference histories, including coupled exchanges, against declared timing rules, reporting missing timing data and exceeded synchronization limits.
requirements.FR-32: The framework shall check exchanged, simulated and supplied reference histories for entity/channel identity, units, timing, completeness and validity before numerical use, preserving raw values, invalid samples, missing intervals and processing masks without treating missing or inactive readings as zero.
requirements.FR-33: The framework shall retain revision-linked modeled EPS interfaces and command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions with endpoint ownership, directions, identifiers, types, units, ranges, polarity, time/mode meaning and encodings.
requirements.FR-34: The framework shall produce or coordinate checked mappings of the EPS interface specification to the required versioned F Prime host integration profile, covering component, port, topology, command, telemetry, event and parameter definitions and identifying version compatibility, unsupported behavior and lossy translations.
requirements.FR-35: The framework shall specify and check modeled EPS command preconditions, order, effects, rejection/failure behavior, mode transitions, protection and recovery responsibilities against the declared control and interface requirements.
requirements.FR-36: The framework shall coordinate coding and host building of declared F Prime EPS control/interface flight software through an external toolchain only from a current engineer-authorized detailed design release, retaining source/build revisions, toolchain versions, dependencies, host configuration, logs and failures.
requirements.FR-19: The framework shall execute and assess MIL scenarios covering nominal operation, supply/load steps, direct energy transfer, MPPT/end-of-charge transitions, command/mode changes, overcurrent/undervoltage/overvoltage faults, interruption, hysteresis, load shedding and recovery. It shall assess model-supported fault detection and diagnosis using simulated or supplied histories, retaining stimuli, expected/actual responses, criteria, alternative fault hypotheses, assessment evidence and failures.
requirements.FR-24: The framework shall execute the simulated EPS plant coupled to external spacecraft/subsystem simulations in the same identified NVIDIA Omniverse scenario under the declared mission/scenario configuration and coupling-profile revisions, coordinate released F Prime host software execution, and assess SIL responses against requirement/ConOps criteria and corresponding MIL results under fixed scenarios and comparison rules, retaining outcomes, differences and limits.
requirements.FR-28: The framework shall retain EPS phase-product verification and validation plans with distinct requirement and expectation/ConOps references, subject configuration, method, conditions, inputs, expected response, criteria, observations, applicability limits and planned/executed status.
requirements.FR-05: The framework shall identify reciprocal impacts of a proposed mission, requirement, component, interface, model or software change on EPS/non-EPS allocations, budgets, trades, plans, guidance and evidence, reporting unresolved dependencies and required reassessments.
requirements.FR-06: The framework shall issue a distinct successor baseline only for an authorized engineering change decision, preserving its predecessor, request, rationale, findings and dispositions and identifying regenerated, stale and unresolved products and evidence.
requirements.FR-07: The framework shall retain retrievable phase baselines that resolve exact requirement, mission, design, model, software, interface and evidence revisions with revision history and the authorized decisions that control them.
requirements.FR-08: The framework shall check transferred identities, revisions, structure, quantities, units, polarity, time/mode meanings and provenance against the declared interface specification before registration, retaining incompatible raw submissions and findings without replacing controlled content.
requirements.FR-09: The framework shall associate each analysis or software result with its requirement/expectation, method, scenario, design/model/software/input revisions, parameters, producer, execution environment, raw outputs, logs and execution status, preserving failed, cancelled and partial runs.
requirements.FR-10: The framework shall provide the controlled inputs, dependencies and instructions to reconstruct a designated analysis or MIL/SIL run and compare its raw outputs using result-specific rules and tolerances fixed before replay, retaining comparison failures and missing dependencies.
requirements.FR-11: The framework shall report missing, rejected, stale, failed, out-of-domain and unresolved evidence against the affected requirements, expectations and conclusions with criticality, owner and disposition, preventing unqualified current conformity claims from affected critical gaps.
requirements.FR-37: The framework shall generate filtered mission, requirement-allocation, design, interface and analysis views from controlled EPS records with baseline identification, readable units, legends and links to represented records.
requirements.FR-38: The framework shall assemble a phase-baseline review package against the designated MCR, SRR, MDR/SDR, PDR, scoped CDR or scoped SIR entrance and success criteria, including applicable coverage, decisions, design, evidence, model limits, risks, gaps and finding dispositions.
requirements.FR-42: The framework shall record a technical review disposition only from the designated authorized review authority against the identified baseline and agreed scoped success criteria, distinguishing prepared, accepted, conditional and progression-blocked status with rationale, conditions, closure actions, owners and dates.
